decisions.reason: Devore decoration fabrics are fashion-driven and may rotate out of the collection after three years, but the variants cost little to hold in a stocked warehouse and the firm promises reorder continuity, so the option stays open until sales clearly disappoint.
This transparent burnout fabric is a trend item with uncertain lasting demand, but with no evidence of failure and low carrying costs it is worth keeping for now.
This burnout decoration fabric overlaps with B and could be pruned in a collection refresh, but there is no signal yet that its value is unrealizable, so it is kept.
Velour-like upholstery fabrics have steadier, longer-lived demand than trend decoration fabrics and fit the firm's upholstery line, so the option remains valuable.
A flame-retardant plain inbetween fabric is a staple for contract and retail buyers with recurring reorders, giving it a low keeping cost and stable value.
Polyester satin lining is a basic continuity article that supports the made-to-measure sewing service and costs little to stock, so dropping it is unlikely.
